title: Fluorescent Staining of T5-phages
author: Unknown
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.iksccwe
materials: After incubation, increase the volume to 1.4 mL
Suspend the viruses in Milli-Q water undetermined

steps.title: Pellet phage (first spin)
steps.instruction: Pellet phage in a SW‑28 rotor ultracentrifuge at 28,000 rpm for 90 min at 10 °C using 35 mL polycarbonate tubes filled to the rim; balance tubes with phage buffer so mass difference is <0.01 g; rotor must be pre‑cooled in the refrigerator.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the resulting pellet in phage buffer (volume not specified).

steps.title: Filter if debris present
steps.instruction: If visible cellular debris remains, filter the resuspension through a 1 mL syringe fitted with a 0.2 µm pore‑size syringe filter.

steps.title: Re‑pellet viruses (second spin)
steps.instruction: Re‑pellet the viruses in a Beckmann TL‑100 ultracentrifuge using the TL‑55 rotor (pre‑cooled) at 35,000 rpm for 2 h at 6 °C in 1.4 mL polycarbonate tubes; fill and balance the tubes as described in step 1.

steps.title: Resuspend and transfer to tubes
steps.instruction: Resuspend the second pellet in phage buffer (volume not specified) and transfer the suspension into 1.5 mL screw‑cap tubes.

steps.title: Add YO‑PRO stain
steps.instruction: Add YO‑PRO stain to each tube containing 100 µL of the resuspended phage (stain volume not specified); perform this step in the dark because the stain is photosensitive.

steps.title: Incubate in dark at 4 °C
steps.instruction: Cover the tubes with aluminum foil and incubate at 4 °C for 48 h.

steps.title: Final centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the stained samples in the Beckmann TL‑100 using the same conditions as step 4 (35,000 rpm, 2 h, 6 °C).
